conventions: Times are ISO 8601 with offset; compare instants, not strings. Grid math runs in UTC (whole-hour zones only).
snap(t) = the grid mark g with g - 15 min < t <= g + 5 min, for start and finish taps alike.

One exception at the planned end E: a finish is on time only in (E - 5 min, E + 5 min]. A finish tap in (E - 15 min, E - 5 min], which snap() would put at E, records E - 20 min instead (the last bar is lost).
Event intervals are half-open [start, end): an event ending at 15:00 does not overlap one starting at 15:00.
Calendar entries carry kind: cadenza or tutti. Only Cadenzas are timed, so snap, start, finish and tokens cases always describe a Cadenza.
A Cadenza may not overlap another Cadenza. Tuttis may overlap anything, without limit.

tapped_at = null in finish cases means the auto-finish job fired at planned_end + 5 min. A finish tap after planned_end + 5 min is rejected with window_closed. Replacing an auto-finish with a late-arriving tap is service behaviour, tested in the backend's integration tests, not here.
Conflict and warning ID lists are sorted. Expected objects must match exactly (no extra keys).
Events with status missed are ignored by overlap checks and cascades. There is no cancelled status: deleted events are gone.
In create cases, event_id (when present) names an existing event being edited; it is left out of its own overlap check.

In create cases, now (when present) is the server's clock. A Cadenza whose start is set before now is rejected with start_in_past; edits that keep the start, and Tuttis, are not checked. Cases without now skip this check.
Calendar entries without a status are planned. A start fails with cadenza_in_progress while another Cadenza is in_progress.
